main_text.head: SECT. IX.
main_text.p: Cùm ergo dico Juramentum esse stri-cti juris, id ita intelligendum est, Jura-menti sententiam ubi ea ex verbis satis manifesta est, omnino tenendam esse: aut ubi sententia dubia est, unicuique se-dulò cavendum, ne nobis nostrisque affectibus nimium indulgeamus, aut ni-mis liberam laxámque interpretandi li-centiam nobismetipsis concedamus, quò facilius nos vinculo juramenti quo obli-gati sumus eximamus; néve sensum ali-quem juramento à nobis præstito aut e-jus alicui parti affingamus, proprii com-modi aut utilitatis causâ, quem non quivis vir alius pius & prudens (qui est liberioris judicii, utpote cujâ nihil in-terest) ex ipsis verbis facilè eliceret.

Ratio duplex. Altera respectu aliorum, ob metum sc. scandali: nequis alius in-firmior nostro exemplo adductus, quod à nobis factum videt id sibi quoque licere putet, etsi ignaro illarum subtilita-tum, quibus tamen solis nosmetipsos à perjurii crimine tueri solemus. Altera respectu nostri ipsorum, ob metum sc. Perjurii: quod gravissimum crimen sine dubio

page.notes: No printed marginal notes. The right margin shows only bleed-through and scan edge marks, which were left out. "Ratio duplex." was treated as a new paragraph because the preceding line ends well short of the margin. The text ends with "dubio" as a catchword, and the italics are as printed. The word "cujâ" is printed with a circumflex and is copied as such.
